On Tue, May 30, 2028 at 09:37 AM Emma Jones <emma.jones@orbishealth.com> wrote:
> Can you confirm which elements are considered ephemeral (never written to disk) vs. persisted to storage?

Hi Emma — quick technical answers (summarized; I filled the spreadsheet with specifics):

- Ephemeral: KV cache (model context cache) and in-flight token buffers are in-memory and not persisted by default. They are lost on instance recycle.
- Persisted: user-requested storage such as long-term prompt logs, user embeddings (if explicitly requested via the embeddings API with persistence enabled), and customer artifacts are written to the configured object store. By default we do not persist full prompts for hosted accounts unless the customer enables prompt logging.
- Logs: application and audit logs capture metadata (request id, model version, token counts) by default. Prompt text logging is off by default for the hosted environment but can be enabled for debugging; for Orbis we will keep that off unless you ask otherwise.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS & GCP CMEK). CMKs can be region-restricted; for a U.S.-only configuration you can provide a key in us-east-1 and we will keep encrypted objects bound to that key in-region.
- Cross-region failover: we offer a warm-standby model where a secondary cluster maintains model weights and a limited cold cache. It does not contain a persisted copy of PII by default. Failover sequence: automatic health detect -> redirect new traffic to standby -> slow sync of KV cache (empty) -> background replay for warmed state. RPO: configurable, typical configuration for Dedicated is 15 minutes; RTO: target 5 minutes for routing cutover, degraded performance until cache warms.
- Backups: snapshots are taken daily and, for U.S.-only profiles, stored in the customer's designated U.S. bucket/encryption boundary. Cross-region snapshot replication is an opt-in for disaster recovery and would replicate encrypted artifacts to the chosen DR region.

I've attached the SLA playbook we discussed with concrete options labeled (see redwood-sla-playbook-v1.pdf) and populated the spreadsheet with the exact fields Orbis requested. Happy to walk through any item during the workshop.

—Ben

Emma — thanks for the questions and great follow-up. Quick summary and proposed schedule: 

- Summary of our commitments (high level):
  • Production data residency: U.S. only (we will pin your account to us-east-1 by default).
  • Prompt logging: disabled for Orbis unless you explicitly enable it.
  • CMK: supported; keys can be region-bound to us-east-1.
  • Backups & snapshots: stored in your U.S. bucket by default; cross-region replication is opt-in.
  • Failover: warm-standby model with configurable RPO (typical 15 min) and RTO target 5 min for routing cutover.

- Deliverables we will prepare before the workshop:
  1) Evidence bundle: SOC2 excerpts, KMS configuration template, and architecture diagram (we'll drop these into the Drive link).
  2) A redlined SLA/playbook that calls out retention windows and failover runbooks (attached PDF).
  3) Updated spreadsheet with boolean toggles for prompt logging, embedding persistence, and cross-region replication (completed).

Proposed workshop windows: June 2 (10:00–11:00 PT) or June 5 (14:00–15:00 PT). Please confirm which works best for your SecOps and we will send calendar invites + an agenda.

If you approve, Ben and I will run the workshop and then provision a U.S-only pilot environment for Orbis the week of June 12.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.
